/**
 * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

00001| --- 00002| title: Migrating to Cache Components 00003| nav_title: Migrating to Cache Components 00004| description: Learn how to migrate from route segment configs to Cache Components in Next.js. 00005| related: 00006| title: Next Steps 00007| description: Learn about other behavior changes when Cache Components is enabled. 00008| links: 00009| - app/guides/optimizing-the-static-shell 00010| - app/guides/instant-navigation 00011| - app/guides/preserving-ui-state 00012| - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components 00013| - app/getting-started/caching 00014| --- 00015| 00016| When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). 00017| 00018| The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. title: Migrating to Cache Components
nav_title: Migrating to Cache Components
description: Learn how to migrate from route segment configs to Cache Components in Next.js.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn about other behavior changes when Cache Components is enabled.
  links:
    - app/guides/optimizing-the-static-shell
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/guides/preserving-ui-state
    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
    - app/getting-started/caching
---

When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife).

The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight.

## Use the adoption skill (recommended)

title: Migrating to Cache Components
nav_title: Migrating to Cache Components
description: Learn how to migrate from route segment configs to Cache Components in Next.js.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn about other behavior changes when Cache Components is enabled.
  links:
    - app/guides/optimizing-the-static-shell
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/guides/preserving-ui-state
    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
    - app/getting-started/caching
---

When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife).

The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight.

## Use the adoption skill (recommended)

00036| - The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`

00033| When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:
00034| 
00035| - The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
00036| - The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
00037| - The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
00038| 
00039| > **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).
00040| 
00041| Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.
00042| 
00043| Read [Prerendering](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) for how the static shell and streaming fit together.
00044| 
00045| > **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating.
00046| 
00047| ## Navigation with Activity
00048| 
00049| When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.
00050| 
00051| Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means:
00052| 
00053| - Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
00054| - When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact
00055| - Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again
00056| 
00057| This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.
00058| 
00059| > **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth.
00060| 
00061| Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for handling common patterns like dropdowns, dialogs, and testing.
00062| 
00063| ## Version History
00064| 
00065| | Version | Change                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
00066| | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00067| | 16.0.0  | `cacheComponents` stabilized and moved from `experimental.cacheComponents` to the top-level `cacheComponents` option. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. |

The `cacheLife` function is used to set the cache lifetime of a function or component. It should be used alongside the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive, and within the scope of the function or component.

## Usage

### Basic setup

To use `cacheLife`, first enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:

The `cacheLife` function is used to set the cache lifetime of a function or component. It should be used alongside the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive, and within the scope of the function or component.

## Usage

### Basic setup

To use `cacheLife`, first enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:

title: use cache
description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application.

The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.

> **Good to know:**
>

This means you can return JSX elements but cannot accept them as arguments unless using pass-through patterns. 00156| 00157| ### Supported types 00158| 00159| **Arguments:** 00160| 00161| - Primitives: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`, `undefined` 00162| - Plain objects: `{ key: value }` 00163| - Arrays: `[1, 2, 3]` 00164| - Dates, Maps, Sets, TypedArrays, ArrayBuffers 00165| - React elements (as pass-through only) 00166| 00167| **Return values:** 00168| 00169| - Same as arguments, plus JSX elements 00170| 00171| ### Unsupported types 00172| 00173| - Class instances 00174| - Functions (except as pass-through) 00175| - Symbols, WeakMaps, WeakSets 00176| - URL instances 00177| 00178| ```tsx filename="app/components/user-card.tsx" 00179| // Valid - primitives and plain objects 00180| async function UserCard({ 00181| id, 00182| config, 00183| }: { 00184| id: string 00185| config: { theme: string } 00186| }) { 00187| 'use cache' 00188| return
{id}

{user.name}

{/* ... */}
00232| } 00233| ``` 00234| 00235| ## Constraints 00236| 00237| Cached functions execute in an isolated environment. The following constraints ensure cache behavior remains predictable and secure. 00238| 00239| ### Request-time APIs 00240| 00241| Cached functions and components **cannot** access runtime APIs like `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams`, and the restriction follows the call stack: a helper the cached function calls that reads one of these fails the same way, with the [`next-request-in-use-cache`](/docs/messages/next-request-in-use-cache) error. On a dynamically rendered route this surfaces when the route runs, so it can pass `next build` and fail under `next start`. Read these values outside the cached scope and pass them as arguments. 00242| 00243| ### Runtime caching considerations 00244| 00245| While `use cache` is designed primarily to include uncached data in the static shell, it can also cache data at runtime using in-memory LRU (Least Recently Used) storage. 00246| 00247| With the default in-memory handler, runtime cache behavior depends on your hosting environment: 00248| 00249| | Environment | Runtime Caching Behavior | 00250| | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | 00251| | **Serverless** | Cache entries typically don't persist across requests (each request can be a different instance), or during revalidation. Build-time caching works normally. | 00252| | **Self-hosted** | Cache entries persist across requests. Control cache size with [`cacheMaxMemorySize`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheMaxMemorySize). | 00253| 00254| For example, in a serverless environment, a cached function shared by two pages executes on each static shell revalidation, whereas in self-hosted or environments with persistent memory, the cached output is reused if it's still fresh. 00255| 00256| If the default in-memory cache isn't enough, consider **[`use cache: remote`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote)** which allows platforms to provide a dedicated cache handler (like Redis or KV database). 'https://draft.example.com/content' 00280| : 'https://production.example.com/content' 00281| 00282| const data = await fetch(url) 00283| return
{/* ... */}
00284| } 00285| ``` 00286| 00287| Calling `enable()` or `disable()` inside a caching directive scope will also throw an error. {shared.current}
00312| } 00313| ``` 00314| 00315| This isolation ensures cached functions have predictable, self-contained behavior. To pass data into a `use cache` scope, use function arguments instead. 00316| 00317| ## `use cache` at runtime 00318| 00319| On the **server**, cache entries are stored in-memory and respect the `revalidate` and `expire` times from your `cacheLife` configuration. You can customize the cache storage by configuring [`cacheHandlers`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers) in your `next.config.js` file. 00320| 00321| On the **client**, content from the server cache is stored in the browser's memory for the duration defined by the `stale` time. The client router enforces a **minimum 30-second stale time**, regardless of configuration. 00322| 00323| The `x-nextjs-stale-time` response header communicates cache lifetime from server to client, ensuring coordinated behavior. 00324| 00325| ## Revalidation 00326| 00327| Cached functions revalidate based on the `revalidate` and `expire` times in their `cacheLife` profile, or on-demand through tags. These two approaches are not mutually exclusive and are often paired: 00328| 00329| - **[Time-based](#time-based-revalidation)**: refresh automatically after a set duration with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). 00330| - **[On-demand](#on-demand-revalidation)**: invalidate after a mutation with [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) and [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) or [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag). 00331| 00332| For example, a blog post that changes only when its author edits it can use a long `cacheLife` like `max` with a `cacheTag`, then invalidate on demand when the post is saved. You might want to cache a network request, a database query, or a slow computation. 00399| 00400| ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" highlight={2} switcher 00401| export async function getData() { 00402| 'use cache' 00403| 00404| const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 00405| const data = await res.json() 00406| return data 00407| } 00408| ``` 00409| 00410| ```jsx filename="app/actions.js" highlight={2} switcher 00411| export async function getData() { 00412| 'use cache' 00413| 00414| const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 00415| const data = await res.json() 00416| return data 00417| } 00418| ``` 00419| 00420| ### Caching a component's output with `use cache` 00421| 00422| You can use `use cache` at the component level to cache any fetches or computations performed within that component. The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.
